sections.heading: M1: System, Model, And Simulation
sections.summary: A system is a collection of interacting or interdependent elements working toward an end. A model represents that system physically, mathematically, or logically, while a simulation imitates its operation over time or space. Modeling and simulation is a problem-based discipline for repeatedly testing hypotheses and supporting decisions. Its four precepts are modeling, simulation, visualization, and analysis.

key_terms.definition: The subject being investigated, including relevant people, hardware, software, facilities, policies, and documents.
A representation of a system, entity, phenomenon, or process.
Using or executing a model to investigate behavior.
A proposed physical system that does not yet exist.

properties.statement: Choose the actual system or a model; choose a physical or mathematical model; for a mathematical model choose analytical evaluation or simulation.

sections.heading: M1: Boundaries, Components, And Modeling Principles
sections.summary: The boundary decides which activities belong to the system and which come from its environment. Entities are objects, attributes are their properties, and activities change the system; the state records the relevant condition at one time. Establish the structure first, then supply attribute values and activity relationships as data. Model only what the study needs, using accurate information and an appropriate amount of aggregation.

A property of an entity.
A process causing system changes.

sections.heading: M1: Study Process, Solutions, And Supporting Disciplines
sections.summary: Analytical methods use mathematics to obtain exact or general results under a model's assumptions when the model is tractable. Simulation evaluates configured scenarios numerically when interactions or constraints make analysis difficult. Both require a sound model, and simulation is not automatically cheap, quick, or random. A useful study repeatedly defines the problem, builds and checks the model, experiments, and interprets results.

key_terms.definition: Mathematical evaluation using algebra, calculus, or probability.
Checking that implementation correctly represents its specified model.
Checking model suitability for the real purpose.
Turning generated data into interpretable performance information.

properties.name: Seven-Step Simulation Process
properties.statement: 1 Define problem; 2 introduce important variables; 3 construct simulation model; 4 specify values to test; 5 conduct simulation; 6 examine results; 7 select best course of action. Revisit model or test values when results require it.

sections.heading: M1: Classifications, Paradigms, And Model Detail
sections.summary: Classifications answer different questions, so a model can be dynamic, stochastic, and discrete at the same time. Monte Carlo emphasizes random sampling, continuous simulation follows continuously evolving states, and discrete-event simulation changes state at event times. Fidelity measures realism, resolution measures detail, and scale measures the size of the represented scenario. Choose the paradigm and detail needed for the question rather than assuming more detail is always better.

key_terms.definition: Closeness to reality for the intended behavior.
Granularity or degree of detail.
Size or level of the overall scenario.
Combining more than one modeling paradigm.

High resolution does not ensure high fidelity.
The page 47 games are illustrative slide comparisons, not universal rankings of realism.

sections.heading: M1: Participation, Applications, And Domains
sections.summary: Participation categories distinguish who acts and whether the operated systems are real or simulated. Applications describe why the simulation is built, while domains describe the subject area. Constructive simulations still receive real human inputs even though their represented actors and systems are simulated. The same domain can support training, analysis, experimentation, engineering, or acquisition.

sections.heading: M1: MATLAB Workspace, Variables, And Classes
sections.summary: MATLAB means Matrix Laboratory and provides computation, visualization, and programming in a matrix-based language. The Command Window accepts commands, the workspace shows variables, the Current Folder shows files, and Command History records earlier commands. Numeric values default to double, while casts deliberately select other numeric, character, or logical classes. MATLAB needs no imports for the built-in commands taught here.

key_terms.definition: Variables available in the active execution context.
The data type of an array.
Conversion using a class function such as int32(num).
A one-element, 1-by-1 array.

properties.name: Help And Session Commands
properties.statement: Exact command names: demo; help; help help; lookfor; doc; quit; exit. demo/doc open help interfaces, help explains functions, lookfor searches help, and quit/exit end MATLAB. These are reference syntax, not replay checks.

properties.name: Page 80 Command-History Expressions

properties.statement: who lists names; whos includes size/bytes/class. Exact slide cleanup syntax: clear; clear variablename; clear variablename1 variablename2. Slide trace: mynum = 3; mynum + 5; clear mynum. These workspace-dependent commands are documented, not used for output checks.

properties.statement: Numeric classes: single, double; signed int8, int16, int32, int64; unsigned uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64. Text shown with single quotes is char; logical stores true/false. sections.heading: M1: MATLAB Operators, Functions, And Special Values
sections.summary: Operators distinguish assignment, comparison, logical decisions, and numerical calculation. Parentheses make precedence explicit and help prevent accidental changes in meaning. Many mathematical functions act elementwise, but reduction functions follow separate dimension rules. Character encoding examples use ASCII values, although MATLAB character handling is not limited to ASCII.

key_terms.definition: The = operator stores a value.
Relational operators return logical results.
&& and || evaluate scalar conditions and can skip an unnecessary right-hand operand.
log(x) is the logarithm to base e, not the value e.

properties.name: Arithmetic And Delimiters
properties.statement: Exact taught syntax: +, -, *, /, \, ^, .*, ./, .\, .^, :, (), [], ., ..., comma, semicolon, %, =, apostrophe ('), and dot-apostrophe (.'). % begins a comment outside text; within fprintf format text it introduces conversion specifications. ... continues a statement onto the next line.

properties.name: Relational And Logical Syntax
properties.statement: <, <=, >, >=, ==, ~=; &&, ||, ~, xor. Slide expressions: 3 < 5; 2 > 9; 2 < 4 || 'a' == 'c'; xor(3 < 5, 'a' > 'c'). Use parentheses, then powers, unary operations, multiplication/division, addition/subtraction, relations, AND, OR as the practical slide precedence order.

properties.name: Rounding And Remainders
properties.statement: fix(x) truncates toward zero; floor(x) rounds down; ceil(x) rounds up; round(x) rounds to nearest. mod(x,n) and rem(x,n) are remainder functions with different negative-argument conventions. Exact slide syntax includes rem(13, 5) and nthroot(64, 3).

properties.name: Functions And Units
properties.statement: sign(x) is -1, 0, or 1 for negative, zero, positive real values; sqrt(x), nthroot(x,n), log(x), log2(x), log10(x), exp(x), sin(x), sind(x), abs(x). sin uses radians and sind uses degrees.

sections.heading: M1: Vectors, Matrices, And Indexing
sections.summary: A matrix has rows and columns, while a vector has only one row or one column. Construct rows using spaces or commas and separate rows using semicolons. MATLAB indexing starts at one and gives row before column for matrix subscripts. size, length, and numel answer different questions and should not be interchanged.

key_terms.definition: A 1-by-n array.
An n-by-1 array.
An element index, starting at 1.
Joining compatible arrays along a dimension.

sections.heading: M1: Reshaping, Rearrangement, And Reductions
sections.summary: Rearrangement changes shape or positions without changing the values being represented, while replication makes copies. reshape preserves MATLAB's columnwise linear order and must preserve the element count. Mathematical functions such as sin and sign usually act elementwise, but sum, prod, min, and max reduce along a dimension. For ordinary matrices with multiple rows, these reductions work down columns by default; specifying dimension two works across rows.

key_terms.definition: Reinterpret the same elements with new dimensions.
Combine several entries into fewer values.
Running totals/products that preserve vector length.
Tiling copies into a larger array.

properties.statement: Exact slide syntax: mat = randi(100,3,4); reshape(mat,2,6); fliplr(mat); flipud(mat); rot90(mat); intmat = randi(100,2); repmat(intmat,3,2);. randi output is random; reuse a saved matrix instead of expecting the same values on each call.

properties.statement: Slide examples: vec = -2:1; sinvec = sin(vec); mat = [0 4 -3;-1 0 2]; sign(mat);. This size-preserving rule does not cover every MATLAB function.

sections.heading: M1: Array Operations And Matrix Algebra
sections.summary: Scalar multiplication or division scales each array element. Array multiplication, division, and power use a dot so that corresponding elements are combined. A row-by-column sum of products.
A scalar property of a square matrix.

sections.heading: M2: Sets And Functions
sections.summary: Sets describe which outcomes belong together before probability is assigned. Union collects either set, intersection keeps the overlap, and difference removes the second set from the first. A function assigns exactly one output to each input; it has an inverse on its full codomain only when it is both one-to-one and onto.

key_terms.definition: A collection of distinct objects; x ∈ S means x belongs to S. The empty set ∅ has no elements.

A finite count terminates, including the empty set; an infinite one does not. Countable includes finite and countably infinite sets; the slide definition using all positive integers describes the latter.
A ⊆ B means every A element is in B. Disjoint sets have no common elements. Equal sets contain exactly the same elements.
The reference collection within which complements are taken.
The domain contains allowed inputs, codomain contains allowed outputs, and range contains outputs actually reached.
Both one-to-one (distinct inputs give distinct outputs) and onto (range equals codomain).

sections.heading: M2: Probability Spaces And Distribution Functions
sections.summary: A probability space separates possible outcomes, permitted events, and the probabilities assigned to those events. A random variable turns an outcome into a real number. key_terms.definition: Sample space S, sigma-algebra A of events, and probability measure P.
A random experiment has an outcome not predictable beforehand; an event is a measurable subset of its sample space.
Contains S and is closed under complements and countable unions, hence also countable intersections.
A measurable function X:S→R: {s:X(s)≤x} belongs to A for every real x.
F(x)=P(X≤x), defined for every real x and taking values in [0,1].
A nonnegative density with integral 1; F(x)=∫ from -∞ to x of f(t)dt.

properties.name: Probability rules
properties.statement: P(E)≥0; P(S)=1; disjoint event probabilities add. The complete measure axiom is countable additivity.

properties.name: CDF rules
properties.statement: F(-∞)=0, F(+∞)=1, 0≤F≤1, F is nondecreasing and right-continuous, and P(a<X≤b)=F(b)-F(a).

properties.name: Density rules
properties.statement: For an absolutely continuous distribution f=dF/dx where the derivative exists; ∫f=1 and P(a<X≤b)=∫ from a to b of f(x)dx. The discrete die uses probability masses instead.

properties.name: Exact die CDF

sections.heading: M2: Input Modeling And Output Analysis
sections.summary: A structural model says what the system contains and how its parts interact; a data model supplies the numerical inputs that make it run. Input streams may replay observations, sample an empirical distribution, or sample a fitted theoretical distribution. Output analysis then turns the resulting observations into evidence about performance rather than treating one random run as the final truth.

key_terms.definition: Defines entities, locations, resources and processes, producing a logical or mathematical system representation.
Supplies interarrival and service durations, schedules, failure rates, travel durations and other quantitative inputs.
Replays stored sample observations.
Nonparametric distribution constructed from the available sample.
Mathematical family with fitted location, scale or shape parameters.
Analysis of simulated observations to describe system performance, including uncertainty in a mean.

properties.name: Choosing a stream
properties.statement: A direct record preserves observed values but may omit rare possibilities and require many retrievals. An empirical distribution supports arbitrary-length sampling but does not recover unobserved extremes. A fitted family smooths sample irregularities and can be efficient, but fitting costs effort and a good fit may not exist.

properties.name: Complex input cases
properties.statement: The picture taxonomy identifies no data, multimodal data, correlated data and nonstationary data. These need more care than choosing an independent stationary one-family fit.

properties.name: Output analysis scope
properties.statement: Page 39 outlines a queue example, confidence interval estimation for a mean, and more complex output cases. It does not teach a detailed confidence-interval calculation or justify treating dependent within-run observations as independent.

worked_examples.problem: Which input strategy fits observed service times that fit no standard family well, when many draws are required?
steps: Replaying a finite record does not by itself give a well-designed fresh stochastic stream.
The slides recommend an empirical distribution when a good theoretical fit cannot be found.
worked_examples.answer: Use an empirical distribution, retaining the limitation that unobserved tail values are not recovered.

common_mistakes: Unlimited draws do not create new knowledge of rare events.
Correlated data should not silently be replaced with independent draws; nonstationary data should not silently use one fixed distribution.

sections.heading: M2: Simulation Executive And Clock Advancement
sections.summary: The executive coordinates initialization, event selection, state updates and final reporting. A next-event list tells the timing routine where to move the simulated clock. properties.name: Next event

sections.heading: M3: Predator-Prey Dynamics And Conservation
sections.summary: Predator and prey populations influence each other through their growth rates. More prey can support predator growth, but more predators suppress prey growth. The parameters and initial populations determine the particular trajectory, rather than the equations specifying a single universal orbit.

A state with both time derivatives zero.

properties.name: Population Equations
properties.statement: dx/dt=x*(b-p*y); dy/dt=y*(r*x-d). Positive parameters: b is intrinsic prey growth, p scales predation, r scales predator growth with prey, d is predator death rate.

properties.name: Positive Equilibrium
properties.statement: For positive populations, b-p*y=0 and r*x-d=0, giving (x*,y*)=(d/r,b/p). With b=p=r=d=1, the positive equilibrium is (1,1). The origin is also an equilibrium but is not the positive coexistence equilibrium.

properties.name: Nine-Stage Slide Cycle

sections.summary: Many continuous-system equations need numerical integration because a convenient analytical solution is unavailable. properties.name: Euler Derivation

properties.statement: t_mid=t0+h/2; x_mid=x0+(h/2)*f(t0,x0); x1=x0+h*f(t_mid,x_mid).

sections.heading: M4: Monte Carlo Fundamentals
sections.summary: Monte Carlo simulation estimates a quantity or output distribution by repeating model evaluations with randomly sampled inputs. Its modern development is associated with 1940s Los Alamos atomic-physics work involving Stanislaw Ulam, Enrico Fermi, John von Neumann and Nicholas Metropolis. Randomness is useful for representing uncertainty, but it does not make Monte Carlo universally better than a deterministic method.

key_terms.definition: Broad class of computational algorithms relying on repeated random sampling for numerical experiments and approximate solutions.
For a fixed input set and fixed model, the evaluation produces a fixed output; random sampling can wrap around that evaluation.
Using possible outcomes and their probabilities to support decisions under uncertainty.
The slide name Stanislaw Ulman refers to Stanislaw Ulam; use Ulam.

properties.name: What is specified
properties.statement: Specify a model, input distributions, sampling assumptions and a quantity to estimate. The desired numerical result need not be known in advance.

properties.name: Statistical basis
properties.statement: Page 5 calls the method not a statistical tool, but Monte Carlo uses probability, statistical sampling and output analysis. It is an algorithmic approach with statistical foundations.

properties.name: Method choice
properties.statement: Monte Carlo handles stochastic input uncertainty and can estimate deterministic quantities such as areas. Direct deterministic methods can be more suitable when tractable and sufficiently accurate.

properties.name: Costs of approximation
properties.statement: The slide advantages are straightforward implementation, computerized sampling, approximate mathematical solutions, and use on stochastic or deterministic problems. The limitations are sampling cost and non-exact answers.

worked_examples.problem: Why simulate a quantity if the slide says its result must be known?
steps: The model and sampling law must be specified, but an unknown mean, probability or integral is the target.

sections.heading: M4: Estimating Pi With A Quarter Circle
sections.summary: Draw points uniformly in the unit square and count those inside the first-quadrant part of a unit circle. The quarter-circle area is π/4 and the square area is one, so the hit fraction estimates π/4. Multiplying that fraction by four gives an estimate of π, not an exact value.

key_terms.definition: The unit square 0≤x≤1 and 0≤y≤1.

key_terms.term: Hit count H and sample count N
key_terms.definition: H counts accepted points; N counts all sampled square points.

properties.name: Estimator
properties.statement: π_hat=4H/N, provided points sample the square uniformly. The pictured numerator refers to a quarter circle even though the formula label says circle.

properties.name: Geometry wording
properties.statement: Use the region inside the quarter-circle arc, not just the arc boundary. The square bounds the quarter-circle region; the area is πr^2/4, not πr^2.

properties.name: Executable sampling pattern, ours
properties.statement: For a fresh repeatable run: rng(1); N=10000; x=rand(1,N); y=rand(1,N); H=sum(x.^2+y.^2<=1); piHat=4*H/N; No particular random-run output is quoted here.

sections.heading: M4: Sensitivity Analysis
sections.summary: Sensitivity analysis asks which uncertain inputs most influence the output and how that influence changes. It can expose model errors, locate important input bounds, focus research and support simplification. Derivative-based methods are computationally efficient, but a derivative describes behavior locally and may not represent the whole range of a nonlinear model.

key_terms.definition: Relates uncertainty in model outputs to sources of input uncertainty.
An input whose uncertainty substantially affects the output quantity being studied.
Rate of output change with input near a specified evaluation point.

properties.name: Why analyze sensitivity
properties.statement: The two slide importance statements cover errors and bounds, then research priorities and model simplification.

properties.name: Linear versus nonlinear
properties.statement: A linear model has constant derivative sensitivity. A nonlinear model can have different sensitivities in different regions, so one local derivative is not a global analysis.

properties.name: Care with the slide wording
properties.statement: The claim that derivatives are of little value for nonlinear behavior is too sweeping. They remain useful locally, but cannot by themselves characterize global nonlinear uncertainty.

sections.heading: M6: Visualization, Graphics Pipeline And Displays
sections.summary: Visualization uses images, graphs, and animation to make information easier to understand. It is especially useful for large datasets and behavior that changes over time, but a convincing image is not proof that the model is valid. Computer graphics supplies the software and hardware that generate and manipulate these images. Follow the graphics pipeline from input through computation to output, keeping the representation, memory, and display jobs separate.

Generation or manipulation of images using computer software and hardware.

properties.statement: The slides trace dedicated workstation graphics acceleration in the mid-1980s, PC 2D acceleration in the mid-1990s, widespread PC 3D fixed pipelines in the late 1990s, and programmable vertex/pixel shaders in the early 2000s.

properties.name: Computation pipeline
properties.statement: Input -> computation -> output. Computation transforms the model, producing a transformed model, then rasterizes it into output image samples. System memory and a frame buffer connect over a system bus with the CPU and video controller; the controller drives the monitor.

properties.name: Input mechanisms
properties.statement: Locator devices return position/orientation, such as tablets/styli, joysticks, and VR trackers. Keyboards supply text/numeric GUI or CAD parameters; hard-coding inserts vertex locations into program code. Scanners and cameras acquire images.

properties.name: Image quality factors

LCDs modulate light rather than emit an electron beam; the cited advantages are flatness, low weight, and low power.

sections.heading: M6: Color, Lighting, Reflection And Shading
sections.summary: Lighting determines how surfaces receive illumination, while reflection describes how light interacts with objects. Shading calculates colors inside polygons, and texture mapping adds surface appearance without greatly increasing geometric complexity. Human rods mainly support low-light vision and cones support color vision. Keep the four light models separate because their position, direction, and falloff assumptions differ.

key_terms.definition: Uniform background illumination independent of location and direction.
An ideal localized source radiating equally in all directions with distance attenuation.
A cone-shaped source specified by location, direction, and cutoff angle.
A distant source modeled by direction and constant intensity rather than finite location.
Mapping image detail to surfaces to enrich appearance without much additional geometry.

properties.name: Visible spectrum
properties.statement: The slides use approximately 380 to 750 nm for visible light. Rods handle low-intensity/night vision; cones provide color vision.

properties.name: Point attenuation
properties.statement: I(Q) = I0/(a+b*d+c*d^2). Here d is light-to-point distance, and a,b,c are constant, linear, and quadratic attenuation coefficients.

properties.name: Spotlight falloff
properties.statement: There is no illumination outside the cutoff cone. Within it the angular factor is commonly cos(phi)^e, where phi is measured from the cone axis and e controls concentration. The formula is cos raised to e, not the cosecant function.

properties.name: Reflection components
properties.statement: The picture contrasts ambient, diffuse, and specular reflection. They describe background response, broadly scattered surface reflection, and concentrated highlights, respectively.

properties.name: Shading methods
properties.statement: Flat shading gives a polygon a uniform shade. Smooth shading interpolates vertex colors. Phong shading interpolates normals for per-point lighting and specular highlights. These are distinct from choosing a texture image.

properties.name: Digital image storage
properties.statement: Images can be stored compressed or uncompressed. Texture detail changes visual appearance without demanding an equivalently detailed polygon mesh.

sections.heading: M6: Verification, Validation And Accreditation
sections.summary: Verification checks whether the model and implementation agree with their specifications. Validation checks whether the representation and its results are sufficiently accurate for the real simuland. Accreditation is an official decision by a responsible authority that the model is acceptable for a specific purpose. Technical V&V evidence informs that decision but does not make the authority or the intended use disappear.

key_terms.definition: Assessment of transformational accuracy across requirements, conceptual model, and executable model.
Assessment of representational accuracy between the simuland, its conceptual representation, and the resulting behavior.
Official certification by a responsible authority that a model is acceptable for a specific purpose.
How likely model results are to be regarded as acceptable for an application.

properties.name: Verification questions
properties.statement: Does program code implement the conceptual model? Does the conceptual model satisfy intended-use requirements? Does the executable model deliver results when needed and in the required format?

properties.name: Validation questions
properties.statement: Does the conceptual model represent the simuland correctly? How close are computed results to actual behavior? Over which inputs are the results credible and useful?

sections.heading: M6: Project Types, Decision Risks And Bounds Of Validity
sections.summary: Different simulation projects have different deliverables and therefore different development priorities. A study seeks insight, software development delivers a reusable executable, and an event applies existing models to a particular objective. Validity also has limits: accepting an invalid or irrelevant model can cause serious harm, while rejecting a valid one wastes potential benefits. Establishing bounds of validity helps prevent unjustified reuse outside the conditions that the evidence supports.

key_terms.definition: A project primarily seeking insight into a simuland; reusable model code need not be the main deliverable.
A project whose primary deliverable is executable simulation software expected to be reused, maintained, and enhanced.
A particular use of existing model(s) for a specified objective.
A valid model is not used; associated with model builder's risk.
An invalid model is used; associated with model user's risk.
A model valid for another purpose is used in an inappropriate application; associated with model accreditor's risk.
The conditions and input domain in which the model is sufficiently accurate for its intended application.

properties.name: Project implications
properties.statement: A study emphasizes findings; software development emphasizes disciplined engineering and long-term maintenance; an event may emphasize scenario development, logistics, database preparation, and security rather than new software.

properties.name: Risk consequences
properties.statement: Type I can waste development costs or delay benefits. Types II and III can produce severe consequences such as improper training or unsafe analyses. The lecture labels them more serious than Type I, not harmless whenever the model once worked elsewhere.

properties.name: Three gravity models exactly as printed

sections.heading: M6: Informal And Static V&V Methods
sections.summary: Informal methods rely strongly on expert observation and reasoning rather than detailed quantitative analysis. Inspection compares project artifacts, whereas face validation compares behavior with experts' knowledge of the simuland. Static methods examine model characteristics without executing a simulation. The method name matters less than knowing what is compared and whether the question is implementation correctness or real-system representation.

key_terms.definition: An informal verification method comparing artifacts such as code, equations, algorithms, and design documents.
An informal validation method comparing simulation behavior with knowledgeable observers' expectations.
A specialized face-validation approach for models of human behavior.
Assessment of model characteristics without executing a simulation.
Static verification of data definitions, allowed ranges, structures, operations, dependencies, and flows.
Static validation comparing important causal relationships in the simuland and conceptual model.

properties.name: Inspection process
properties.statement: Teams compare artifacts using expertise, identify potential faults, assess them, and prioritize them. Inspections can be ad hoc or structured; structured teams may assign moderator, reader, and recorder roles.

properties.name: Face validation evidence
properties.statement: Potential users or subject-matter experts observe outputs under given conditions and judge acceptability using their knowledge. It is common in interactive virtual simulations, and may be used when data or time for more objective methods are scarce.

properties.name: Turing test focus
properties.statement: The test concerns modeled human behavior and human expectations. It is a specialized face-validation method, not an accreditation certificate or proof of general correctness.

properties.name: Data definitions and operations
properties.statement: Check data types, allowable ranges, and appropriate operations. Data dependency analysis asks which variables depend on which others; data flow analysis asks what is passed between executable-model modules.

properties.name: Causal graphs
properties.statement: Identify important causes/events/conditions and effects/state changes in both simuland and conceptual model. Nodes represent causes/effects and directed edges represent causal relationships; correct missing or extraneous links. Petri nets are mentioned as a widely used diagrammatic modeling notation.

common_mistakes: Inspection is verification, while face validation is validation; do not classify both by the fact that humans participate.
Static means no simulation execution for that assessment, not that the modeled physical system never changes.
The slide's wording about effects connecting nodes is confusing: directed edges express causal relationships.
A convincing human-like output is not proof that every internal equation is implemented correctly.

sections.heading: M6: Dynamic And Formal V&V Methods
sections.summary: Dynamic methods execute the model and assess its results, often using numerical comparisons. Sensitivity analysis studies responses over changing inputs, while predictive validation compares particular corresponding outcomes. Formal methods instead seek mathematical proofs using explicit statements and logical rules. A practical V&V effort normally combines methods selected for the model, the available simuland data, and the feasibility of repeated execution.

key_terms.definition: Accuracy assessment by executing a model and evaluating its results.
Comparing magnitude and variability of model responses with simuland behavior over the same input range; also identifies influential inputs.
Comparing specific corresponding model outcomes and simuland outcomes.
Dynamic verification that runs multiple models of the same simuland with identical inputs and compares outputs.
A statistical technique for relationships between variables; here, a dynamic validation method using paired model and observation values.
A statistical comparison of simulation-result samples with a valid-results distribution, its parameters, or a reference sample.
Use of mathematical statements and proofs to establish model characteristics.
Formal verification proving that path-entry assertions plus executed instructions imply path-exit assertions.
Formal validation expressing properties of simuland and conceptual model and using logical arguments to assess consistency.

properties.name: Sensitivity evidence
properties.statement: Compare response surfaces for appropriately selected independent/input and dependent/output variables. Examine both sign and magnitude of differences and how input errors affect results.

properties.name: Predictive and comparison tests
properties.statement: Predictive validation compares model outputs with corresponding actual outcomes. Comparison testing compares multiple models using the same inputs; agreement alone does not prove that all represent reality correctly.

properties.name: Regression caveat
properties.statement: The lecture describes relatedness and variation between variables and paired comparisons. Statistical association by itself does not establish causation or eliminate bias shared by model and observations.

properties.name: Hypothesis-testing setup
properties.statement: Treat multiple relevant simulation results as a sample from the population of possible model outcomes. Choose an appropriate test and compare with accepted valid results; a single pleasing plot is not that test.

properties.name: Inductive proof structure
properties.statement: For each possible execution path, prove that a true starting assertion and the path instructions imply the ending assertion. Mathematical induction supports the correctness argument relative to the stated specification.

properties.name: Predicate proof scope
properties.statement: Describe properties of the simuland and conceptual model in formal logic and prove their consistency under the stated premises. A proof based on assumptions does not independently prove the physical truth of those assumptions.

properties.name: Practical method selection
properties.statement: Formal proofs are difficult for complex useful models and more practical in constrained situations. Select methods using model type, available comparison data, and ease of repeated runs; study prior V&V for similar models and combine complementary methods.

common_mistakes: Comparison testing is classified as verification in the slides, not an automatic validation against reality.
Do not confuse repeated simulation samples with a proof of all possible behavior.
Regression association is not proof of causality.
Formal verification of code does not guarantee that its conceptual physics is valid.
One V&V method need not address every concern; the slides explicitly favor combinations when appropriate.

self_check.question: How do system, model, and simulation differ?
self_check.answer: The system is the subject, the model represents it, and simulation operates that model.

self_check.question: Does observing a continuous system once per second make it a discrete system?
self_check.answer: No. This is sampled-data observation of underlying continuous dynamics.

self_check.question: How do fidelity, resolution, and scale differ?
self_check.answer: Realism, detail, and represented scenario size respectively.

self_check.question: What does sum return for a general 2-by-3 matrix, and what about sum(A,2)?
self_check.answer: sum(A) is 1-by-3 column totals; sum(A,2) is 2-by-1 row totals.

self_check.question: What distinguishes A*B from A.*B?
self_check.answer: Matrix multiplication sums row-column products and matches inner dimensions; elementwise multiplication combines corresponding compatible entries.

self_check.question: Which baseline slide corrections are easy exam traps?
self_check.answer: sign(0)=0; log is base e, not equal to e; unsigned integers include zero; page 13 heights are 1084 and 1136 at t=1,2; not every function preserves shape.

self_check.question: What two function properties are required for an inverse on the full codomain?
self_check.answer: One-to-one and onto.

self_check.question: Why is F(2)=1/2 in the three-sided die?
self_check.answer: X≤2 includes B and C, so 1/6+1/3=1/2.

self_check.question: Correct the slide exponential density.
self_check.answer: λexp(-λx) for x≥0, 0 otherwise; λ=1/m.

self_check.question: Why is the page 31 LCG full period?
self_check.answer: gcd(3,20)=1; factors 2 and 5 divide a-1=0; and 4 divides both 20 and 0. Its period is 20.

self_check.question: How do balking, reneging and jockeying differ?
self_check.answer: Not joining, leaving after joining before service, and switching lines respectively.

self_check.question: What are customer 5 wait and system time in the FCFS example?
What is wrong with saying a continuous system has identical constant input and output?
self_check.answer: Continuity concerns time/state evolution, not equality or constancy of input and output.

self_check.question: What is the reservoir state equation, including an initial condition in its integral form?
self_check.answer: dq/dt=x(t); q(t)=q(0)+integral from 0 to t of x(s)ds; output y=q.

self_check.question: What correction is needed in the general predator-prey invariant?
self_check.answer: Replace -x by -r*x: C=b ln(y)-p*y-r*x+d ln(x).

self_check.question: How do Euler and the slide's Runge-Kutta method differ?
self_check.answer: Euler uses the initial slope; the slide shows explicit midpoint RK2, using a predicted midpoint slope.

self_check.question: How do scripts/functions, input/disp/fprintf differ?
self_check.answer: Scripts run in a workspace; functions have formal arguments/results and local internals. input reads, disp displays plainly, fprintf formats output.

self_check.question: What are the selection/loop traps?
self_check.answer: % comments, so use mod for parity and print Odd number in the odd branch; handle age 20 and invalid ages explicitly; 60 already goes to senior. break exits, continue skips the current iteration, and update placement controls while endpoints.

self_check.question: Correct the name Ulman and the claim that the answer must be known.
self_check.answer: Stanislaw Ulam. The model and sampling assumptions are specified; the target result is generally estimated.

self_check.question: List the four process steps in order.
self_check.answer: Define input distributions, generate random inputs, perform deterministic computations, aggregate outputs.

self_check.question: What happens to typical standard error when sample count is quadrupled?
self_check.answer: It halves under ordinary independent finite-variance sampling.

self_check.question: Why is pi estimated by four times the hit fraction?
self_check.answer: The quarter-circle to unit-square area ratio is π/4, so multiply H/N by 4.

self_check.question: Why is a local derivative insufficient for global nonlinear sensitivity?
self_check.answer: The derivative can change across the input range; it describes the selected operating point.

self_check.question: Distinguish axis equal, axis square, save -ascii and load.
self_check.answer: axis equal equalizes unit scales; axis square makes the plot box square. save -ascii writes numeric ASCII; the shown load reads a rectangular ASCII file into a filename-base variable.

self_check.question: How do the four Fishwick types differ?
self_check.answer: Declarative: states/events. Functional: directed equation flow. Constraint: physical relationships/balance. Spatial: spaces or entities in them.

self_check.question: Why do the functional and constraint braking results agree?
self_check.answer: They express the same constant-friction physics: integrating acceleration gives the motion; equating initial energy to friction work gives the same stopping distance.

self_check.question: Is a concept map automatically a hybrid executable model?
self_check.answer: No. A concept map informally explains elements/interactions; a hybrid connects models, potentially of multiple types.

self_check.question: What distinguishes verification from validation?
self_check.answer: Verification checks correct implementation of conceptual requirements. Validation checks useful accuracy against the target system.

self_check.question: Which methods and workflow does the OR slide list?
self_check.answer: Formulate the problem, develop its mathematical model, solve it. Linear programming is deterministic; Markov chains and queuing theory are stochastic methods.

self_check.question: Does page 30 establish a 16-character Hello FEU Tech greeting?
self_check.answer: No. The visible greeting has 14 characters. The lower 16 belongs to a cropped branch whose input text is not established.

self_check.question: What is the difference between a geometric vector and a raster pixel?
self_check.answer: A vector has direction and magnitude; a pixel is an addressable picture element. A vector display traces strokes and is an output technology.

self_check.question: Why do homogeneous points and vectors use different fourth coordinates?
self_check.answer: The shown point w=1 permits translation; a direction vector w=0 is unchanged by pure translation.

self_check.question: How do perspective and orthographic projections differ?
self_check.answer: Perspective projectors meet at a finite COP. Orthographic projectors share a perpendicular DOP and preserve measurements along the projection plane.

self_check.question: What are verification, validation, and accreditation?
self_check.answer: Verification: specification/implementation consistency. Validation: sufficiently accurate representation of the simuland. Accreditation: official acceptance for a specified purpose.

self_check.question: Which errors are builder, user, and accreditor risks?
self_check.answer: Type I: valid model not used, builder risk. Type II: invalid model used, user risk. Type III: irrelevant model used, accreditor risk.

self_check.question: What should be said about page81 model2 and the selection of V&V methods?
self_check.answer: The printed -420/9 slope is inconsistent with its plotted line and claimed t5 to10 accuracy; no unique corrected coefficient is established. Select complementary methods based on model, data, and feasible execution rather than accepting appearance alone.
